blogs.title: When Sepsis Masks a TMA: Unraveling Thrombotic Microangiopathy in the ICU
blogs.description: A step‑by‑step review of how septic patients can develop a superimposed TMA, focusing on red flags that distinguish DIC from complement‑mediated HUS. We’ll discuss the timing of laboratory clues (schistocytes, LDH surge, platelet trends), the utility of PLASMIC scoring, and when to pivot from treating sepsis alone to initiating plasma exchange and complement blockade.

blogs.title: Capnocytophaga canimorsus: The Forgotten Zoonotic Trigger of Complement‑Mediated HUS
blogs.description: An in‑depth look at C. canimorsus infections, their clinical spectrum, and why they should be on every clinician’s differential for severe sepsis after animal bites. The post covers microbiology, culture challenges, the role of rapid molecular diagnostics, and the emerging evidence linking this pathogen to complement activation and atypical HUS.

blogs.title: Eculizumab in the Midst of Infection: Balancing Complement Blockade and Host Defense
blogs.description: Explores the therapeutic dilemma of initiating eculizumab while a patient still harbors bacteremia. We’ll examine infection‑related risks, vaccination timing, prophylactic antibiotics, and real‑world strategies (PEX bridging, culture clearance) using this case as a framework for safe complement inhibition in sepsis‑associated TMAs.

blogs.title: Beyond C3/C4: Advanced Complement Testing and Genetic Workup in Atypical HUS
blogs.description: A practical guide to interpreting complement studies—AH50, factor H/I/B levels, autoantibodies—and when to send extended genetic panels. The article highlights why normal C3/C4 does not rule out CM‑HUS, how plasma exchange and eculizumab affect assay results, and how to integrate genetic findings into long‑term management decisions.

blogs.title: Renal Biopsy in the ICU: When and How to Confirm TMA in a Dialysis‑Dependent Patient
blogs.description: Discusses the indications, timing, and safety considerations for performing kidney biopsies in critically ill patients with AKI and suspected TMA. Using the presented case, we’ll review histopathologic hallmarks of complement‑mediated HUS versus other causes, and how biopsy results can shape therapeutic pathways.

blogs.title: From Bite to Dialysis: A Clinical Timeline Toolkit for Rapid Diagnosis of Infection‑Triggered TMAs
blogs.description: Presents a visual timeline and decision‑making algorithm that maps key clinical events—from animal exposure to haemolysis onset—highlighting when to order specific tests (ADAMTS13, Shiga toxin PCR, complement assays) and start targeted therapies. Designed as a bedside reference for emergency physicians, intensivists, and nephrologists.
